limitations: The requested ApoMarioHighscore class and public methods do not yet exist in the inspected repository, so their exact symbol anchors and implementation-specific parser/store sinks cannot be resolved.
No shared level-server/client implementation was found in the inspected source listing; only local file chooser, replay, property, and binary level-loading paths were traced.

The inspection did not establish a safe elapsed-time source for every editor/custom/replay level; ApoMarioLevel#getPassedTime() directly dereferences randomLevel and requires implementation/test confirmation.
The output identifies existing decoder risks and proposed controls but does not implement or modify the feature.

nodes.label: ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean) is the run-completion aggregation point: it computes time/difficulty/width bonus, changes player points for wins or losses, sets the win flag, and transitions to the analysis panel.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore record must be taken after the final score mutation and before the run state is replaced or reset.
nodes.verification: Exercise both bWin paths and verify the stored score equals the final post-bonus player score.

nodes.label: The human player's displayed name is currently the literal “human”; AI/team names come from ApoMarioPlayer#getTeamName(), while points are exposed by ApoMarioPlayer#getPoints().
nodes.task_relevance: The integration must define which player is recorded and must not silently use an unrelated display value.
nodes.verification: Run with a human player and with an AI player and verify the recorded/displayed names match the selected player identity.

nodes.label: ApoMarioLevel#getPassedTime() derives elapsed time as randomLevel.getTime() minus the current time, while ApoMarioLevel#getTime() is decremented by thinkTime(int); the inspected code does not establish that randomLevel is non-null for every level source.
nodes.task_relevance: Survival-time recording must handle editor/custom/replay levels without dereferencing unavailable timing state.
nodes.verification: Record runs from random, editor, and replay/custom levels and verify elapsed time is finite and non-negative.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject the decoded level and report the rejection; do not allocate arrays for non-positive or over-limit dimensions.
nodes.label: The binary level decoder reads width and height from local file data and immediately allocates new ApoMarioEntity[height][width] without visible bounds checks; a crafted file can cause excessive allocation or failures before the catch block.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore feature consumes run state produced by this decoder, so malformed level inputs can deny service or create invalid timing/score state before recording.
nodes.verification: Supply zero, negative, and oversized dimensions and verify rejection occurs before allocation and the caller reports the failed load.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject invalid records and report the rejection; the caller must use a stated safe level-load fallback while preserving the requested load operation's effect.
nodes.label: The level decoder dispatches on file-controlled entity types and fields, catches broad exceptions, prints a stack trace, and returns false; malformed input is not visibly normalized before entity construction.
nodes.task_relevance: A future run recorder must not treat partially decoded levels or invalid timing/entity state as authoritative highscore input.
nodes.verification: Corrupt each entity-type and field encoding and verify the decoder reports rejection rather than exposing a partial level as valid.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject unsafe or invalid player class input and report the rejection; the integration falls back to the human/default player identity while preserving game startup.
nodes.label: Local player loading derives a class name/path from a user-selected file and passes it to ApoMarioClassLoader, which loads class bytes from a file and defines the class.
nodes.task_relevance: If leaderboard identity reuses AI/team names, the name source can be controlled by a local file and must not be treated as trusted identity.
nodes.verification: Attempt to load a class from an invalid or hostile local path and verify rejection does not prevent the game from starting with a default identity.

nodes.failure_behavior: The highscore parser rejects and reports each invalid file/record; panel initialization uses an empty bounded board so menu operation continues.
nodes.label: A user-editable highscore file could inject malformed, extreme, duplicate, or reordered entries; accepting it directly could corrupt leaderboard integrity, consume memory, or render attacker-controlled text.
nodes.task_relevance: The new ApoMarioHighscore(Path) persistence API is the primary file trust boundary introduced by the feature.
nodes.verification: Use malformed encodings, invalid numeric ranges, oversized names, and excessive record counts; verify rejection is reported and rendering remains bounded.

nodes.failure_behavior: The integration normalizes missing/invalid name and elapsed time before storeRun, then records once after final score calculation; it does not suppress run completion if persistence fails.
nodes.label: Recording before ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis finishes its score mutations, or recording a mutable/incorrect player and time source, could persist a score that does not represent the completed run.
nodes.task_relevance: The task explicitly requires the real score, player name, and survival time on both clearing and losing.
nodes.verification: Test win, timeout, death, replay, and loss paths; assert one record per completed run with final score, selected player name, and non-negative elapsed time.

nodes.failure_behavior: The store rejects records exceeding configured count/name/field limits; the menu renders only the bounded validated list and substitutes a safe display string for missing data.
nodes.label: Persisting unlimited records or displaying unbounded names can cause memory, file-size, or UI denial of service.
nodes.task_relevance: The leaderboard is a persistent menu view and therefore must bound both storage and rendering work.
nodes.verification: Insert more than the configured maximum and names at/over the maximum length; verify rejected entries are reported and rendering remains within fixed bounds.

nodes.failure_behavior: storeRun returns false or otherwise reports rejection and does not add the invalid entry; the run-end caller supplies a stated default/normalized value before calling it so the primary recording effect still occurs.
nodes.label: ApoMarioHighscore#storeRun must validate score, survivalTime, and playerName, enforce finite ranges and bounded name/record sizes, and preserve entries sorted by score descending; invalid input must be rejected and reported rather than substituted or clamped.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects leaderboard integrity and availability at the operation that receives run data.
nodes.verification: Unit-test negative/overflow scores, negative/overflow times, null/blank/oversized names, duplicate scores, and ordering after multiple valid inserts.

nodes.failure_behavior: Invalid file data is rejected and reported; the panel falls back to an empty validated board before menu rendering, preserving menu availability.
nodes.label: The highscore store loader used by ApoMarioHighscore(Path) and persistAcrossRuns must parse a bounded, explicit record format, reject malformed or extra-invalid records with a reported rejection, and expose only validated aligned name/score/time lists.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects persisted leaderboard integrity and prevents malformed local files from poisoning menu state.
nodes.verification: Construct ApoMarioHighscore with nonexistent, truncated, malformed, oversized, and valid stores; verify reported rejection, empty fallback, and aligned validated getters.

nodes.failure_behavior: Before storeRun, the caller substitutes a documented safe default for null/blank name and a non-negative bounded fallback for unavailable/invalid elapsed time; it reports persistence failure but still completes the analysis/menu transition.
nodes.label: The run-end integration must call recordRunEnd(level) only after final score changes for both clearing and losing, read the selected player's actual points and name, derive elapsed survival time from the finished level, and submit one record per run.

nodes.verification: Run win, timeout, death, one-player, two-player, AI, replay, and custom-level scenarios; verify exactly one aligned record and final score/time values.

nodes.failure_behavior: Persistence or rendering errors are reported; the caller retains the in-memory validated board and continues to the menu using bounded fallback rendering.

nodes.verification: Fuzz dimensions, entity types, truncated streams, and timing fields; verify rejection precedes allocation/mutation and the caller reports failure.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return false/report the rejection and leave the validated board unchanged; recordRunEnd normalizes missing values before this call.

summary: ApoMario currently computes player points and run completion in ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis, exposes player names/points and elapsed-time state through ApoMarioLevel, initializes menu/game panels in ApoMarioPanel, and renders menu player data in ApoMarioMenu. Existing file-backed level/replay/property loading accepts local file data at several boundaries. The requested highscore feature introduces a new local persistence store, run-end recording flow, and dedicated menu view; those new operations are not present in the inspected source.
